context: This four-level perfect binary tree has 15 nodes. The root is 1, and the values run from 1 through 15 level by level, left to right. Nodes 8 through 15 on the bottom level are leaves with no children. The table lists the left and right child links for the seven non-leaf nodes, 1 through 7.
description: The orange region encloses the left subtree of root 1, and the blue region encloses its right subtree. Each region includes its own root and all its descendants.

frames.explanation: Relative to root 1, the directly connected left child is the single node 2, and the right child is the single node 3. The left subtree is the entire tree rooted at 2, with 7 nodes: 2, 4, 5, 8, 9, 10, and 11. The right subtree is rooted at 3 and also has 7 nodes: 3, 6, 7, 12, 13, 14, and 15. Each subtree includes its root and all its descendants, extending beyond the child alone in this example.
frames.title: Nodes and subtrees of a binary tree

result: Parent-child and subtree relationships depend on the reference node. Node 1 is the parent of 2 and 3, and 2 is the parent of 4 and 5. The “Parent” label on root 1 describes its relationship to 2 and 3. The root itself has no parent.
summary: The root and its left and right branches illustrate the difference between one directly connected child and the subtree containing that child and all its descendants.

tables.caption: Left and right children of every non-leaf node in the figure

title: Nodes and subtrees of a binary tree
